payload.summary: Production deploys stopped landing for 27 hours on 2026-09-21; root cause unknown and GitHub-issue monitor routing still did not drive action
payload.detail: Second occurrence of the Railway deploy-rollback failure mode first seen 2026-09-11..09-14 (24 consecutive rollbacks, documented in scripts/check-live-deployment-freshness.mjs and docs/deployment-architecture.md 'Readiness: what /api/health/ready may and may not ask'). Measured 2026-09-22 from GitHub deployment statuses: the Database service in the production environment last landed a deploy at 2026-09-21T05:59Z (3a43f808d) and did not land another until 2026-09-22T09:15Z (76bf29ffa, PR #2978). In between, four production deployments were created for ef257fa5c, f44ae5397, 56b123509 and 373046b76 and every one went in_progress -> inactive without ever reaching success. All four built cleanly in the Docker image build workflow, live-drift was green on the 2026-09-21 migrations, and Railway built PR preview environments normally throughout, so the integration, the image and the database are all ruled out. That leaves Railway-side deploy/start/healthcheck rejection, which is the documented mechanism: each healthcheck attempt gets ~10s against /api/health/ready and a container that cannot answer inside the window is discarded and rolled back, leaving the previous deploy serving. Confirming which of the four failed and why needs the Railway deployment logs for the production environment, which no agent session has had access to. Production recovered on its own and no fix was applied, so the trigger is unknown and can recur. Separately confirmed NOT a fault: nine main commits in the same window got a staging deploy but no production deploy at all - all nine touched no path matched by watchPatterns in railway.app.json, which is correct filtering. Alerting clarification (rewrites a false claim in the original draft of this request): live-domain-monitor.yml already has monitor-routing (issues: write + actions/github-script) as of #2884 / ledger #TN512M, and it DID fire during this stall — pinned issue #2973 ('Live domain monitor failing', label live-monitor-failure) was opened 2026-09-21T12:40Z, updated on later red runs including the deployment-freshness failure at 2026-09-22T06:47Z, and closed on the next green run at 2026-09-22T12:41Z. So 'nothing routes a red monitor run' is false. What remains unverified for human delivery: despite #2973 being open and repeatedly commented for ~24 hours of the stall, the gap was still found only because a human inspected GitHub deployment statuses, not because anyone acted on the pinned issue. That matches the #TN512M residual ('Close once a genuine outage has produced a notification someone acted on') and the workflow comment that owner failure emails arrive unread. Durable next actions: (1) pull Railway production deployment logs for the four inactive deploys and record the reject reason; (2) treat this stall as the missing #TN512M real-outage evidence that GitHub-issue routing alone is insufficient delivery, and decide a human-reachable path (page/Slack/owner push) before adding more probes. Pairs with #HYSWAF (Railway deploys every main push without waiting for required checks) and #TN512M.
payload.source: Claude session 2026-09-22; GitHub deployment statuses for Database/production; live-domain-monitor runs 35639421619/35696377977/35728663173 and issue #2973 routing evidence; Codex review on PR #2982
